basis: Anemia defined by enlarged red blood cells; no additional organ damage intrinsic to this umbrella concept.
Corpus callosum malformation and progressive sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and hypotonia; no established direct damage to another organ axis.
Functional gastrointestinal disorder defined by recurrent vomiting; migraine association and broad neuroendocrine ancestry do not establish additional organ disease.
Vascular hamartoma arising in retinal capillaries; both the retina and its abnormal vessels define the lesion.
Purine-synthesis disorder with defining neuropathy and deafness; optic atrophy and progressive visual loss occur in 80-100%. Muscle atrophy is neurogenic.
Limb agenesis; renal agenesis and oral clefts in 2/3; adrenal agenesis in 1/3. Ocular anomalies and asplenia in 1/3 omitted by cap; evidence is a small series.
Vasopressin deficiency is an endocrine disorder; polyuria does not establish intrinsic urinary tract damage.
Defined by brachydactyly and cerebellar dysfunction; nystagmus reflects abnormal ocular motor control without established intrinsic eye damage.
Joint laxity, pectus carinatum and genu valgum define skeletal and connective tissue involvement; facial appearance alone adds no other axis.
Inflammation or mechanical irritation of a synovial bursa; infection and autoimmunity are not intrinsic to bursitis overall.
Benign melanocytic skin nevus with fibrous stroma.
Primary innate immunodeficiency; recurrent meningitis in 5/9 represents separately diagnosed infection rather than intrinsic neurologic disease.
Congenital peripheral hypomyelinating neuropathy; muscle atrophy is neurogenic, and potential respiratory dysfunction does not establish common lung damage.
Schizophrenia subtype is a purely psychiatric disorder; nonspecific nervous system annotation does not establish an additional neurologic disease.
Defined by microcephaly, epilepsy, profound developmental impairment and neonatal diabetes; ocular, renal and skeletal abnormalities are annotated below 30%.
Immunodeficiency with autoinflammation; scoliosis, pectus and limb deformity in 1/1 support skeletal involvement. Single-patient evidence; pneumonia and hypothyroidism are separate diseases.
Autoimmune neuromuscular junction dysfunction; ocular and generalized weakness arise from junctional failure rather than intrinsic eye or muscle disease.
Brainstem and cerebellar malformations define the syndrome; ocular motor and respiratory signs are neurologic. Intrinsic retinal and renal disease do not meet 30% across the umbrella.
Cerebellar ataxia, epilepsy and intellectual disability all fall within the neurologic axis; no shared extra-neurologic organ disease is established.
Epithelial neoplasm arising in the ovary, a reproductive site; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish disease of gonadal hormone-producing tissue.
Severe neonatal urea-cycle disorder; hyperammonemic encephalopathy and brain injury affect most symptomatic neonates, with common lasting neurologic deficits.
Systemic Lassa virus infection; hearing loss and abnormal bleeding are annotated at 5-29%, below threshold. Common pharyngitis does not establish lasting airway damage.
Hyperplasia of urinary tract urothelium; urinary tract epithelium belongs to the renal axis.
Inherited disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis is a disorder of cutaneous keratinization.
